quote: Section 9.2(a) covers *any* breach of or inaccuracy in *any* representation or warranty made by Seller. As drafted, this means the 10% cap ($1,840,000) and the $184,000 basket are both inapplicable to every representation claim—not just Fundamental Representations. ... after the Release Date, Marrowind has unlimited direct exposure. ... Revise § 9.4(c) to: "(c) Exceptions. The limitation set forth in Section 9.4(a) shall not apply to any claim under Section 9.2(a) based on a breach of a Fundamental Representation, or to any claim arising from fraud."
reason: The memo meets each part of the criterion. It names APA § 9.4(c) as the provision that lifts the § 9.4(a) 10% cap for all § 9.2(a) claims. It states that § 9.2(a) reaches any Seller representation, not only fundamental ones. It explains why this matters to Marrowind: uncapped exposure that goes beyond the $1,840,000 escrow. It also recommends limiting the carve-out to Fundamental Representations and fraud. The memo does not propose capping those carved-out claims at the Purchase Price, but the criterion does not require that.
